content: Calmurid is a topical cream produced by the pharmaceutical company Galderma. The standard formulation of Calmurid contains two active ingredients: lactic acid and urea. Lactic acid has keratolytic properties, meaning it helps to break down and remove hardened or thickened skin cells. Urea, on the other hand, has hydrating properties, which help to moisturize and soften the skin. Together, these ingredients make Calmurid effective in managing conditions characterized by dry and scaly skin. Calmurid is commonly prescribed for the treatment of ichthyosis, a condition involving persistently dry, thickened, and scaly skin, as well as for general dermatitis that does not involve inflammation. A variant of this cream, known as Calmurid HC, includes an additional active ingredient: hydrocortisone, a mild corticosteroid. The inclusion of hydrocortisone allows Calmurid HC to address not only dry and scaly skin but also skin conditions accompanied by inflammation. This makes it suitable for treating inflammatory skin conditions such as certain types of eczema. However, due to the presence of the corticosteroid in Calmurid HC, it is important to use this formulation sparingly and for the shortest duration necessary. Prolonged or excessive use of corticosteroids can lead to systemic absorption, which may result in unwanted side effects. Therefore, careful adherence to medical guidance is essential when using Calmurid HC.
